headline: China-linked ransomware crews and Iran-suspected saboteurs race to weaponize freshly patched enterprise and industrial flaws, while attackers learn to turn defensive AI agents against their owners.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now weaponize the tooling meant to catch them, planting commands inside security logs so GhostJacking hijacks the AI agents that triage alerts.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GhostJacking Turns AI Agents Against Defenders

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware affiliates keep turning fresh patches into targets, as the China-linked Storm-1175 crew drops StormEncryptor through the same N-central flaw providers are still hot-fixing.
emerging_trends.topic_title: StormEncryptor Ransomware Hits via N-central Flaw

emerging_trends.text: State-aligned operators keep reaching into physical systems, with intruders tied to Iran hitting internet-exposed controllers at water utilities across a dozen states.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Water Utility Attacks Widen, Iran Suspected

topics.title: StormEncryptor Ransomware Hits via N-central Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft tied StormEncryptor, a new C++ encryptor that appends the .encrypted extension, to Storm-1175, a China-linked crew and former Medusa affiliate that likely breaks in through Progress N-able N-central flaw CVE-2026-18577, which N-able rushed a second hotfix to close.
topics.summary: Storm-1175 abandoned Medusa for its own StormEncryptor strain, hitting managed service providers through the actively exploited N-central bug; administrators must apply N-able's Hotfix 2 and hunt for the shared indicators of compromise.

sources.title: New StormEncryptor ransomware used by former Medusa affiliate
China-Linked Hackers Deploy New StormEncryptor Ransomware, Likely via N-central Flaw
N-able ships second N-central hotfix as attackers keep exploiting CVE-2026-18577

topics.title: Water Utility Attacks Widen, Iran Suspected
topics.latest_developments: Hackers whom investigators tie to Iran extended attacks on internet-exposed programmable logic controllers to water plants in New Jersey and Alabama, carrying the campaign past a dozen states, and Senate Democrats answered with a bill to spend $300 million a year hardening water and wastewater systems.
topics.summary: Iran-linked hackers keep hitting poorly secured, internet-facing industrial controls at U.S. water utilities; operators should pull PLCs off the open internet and enforce authentication, and Congress now weighs dedicated funding.

sources.title: Multistate Water System Attacks Widen, Iran Suspected
New Jersey, Alabama Join States Targeted in Water Cyberattacks
Senate Democrats introduce bill to distribute $300 million annually to shore up water system cybersecurity

topics.title: Metabase Zero-Day Patched After Framework Breach
topics.latest_developments: Metabase shipped a fix for the maximum-severity SQL injection flaw attackers exploited as a zero-day, which still carries no CVE, after Framework, the San Francisco repairable-laptop maker, told customers intruders stole names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, and login IP addresses.
topics.summary: The bug hands unauthenticated remote attackers administrator access to self-hosted Metabase analytics and every downstream data source; run the patched build immediately and assume compromise on exposed instances.

sources.title: Metabase Patches Vulnerability Exploited as Zero-Day
Metabase zero-day exploited to access Framework customer data
Metabase SQL Zero-Day Attacks Could Have Wide Blast Radius

topics.title: GhostJacking Turns AI Agents Against Defenders
topics.latest_developments: Researchers revealed GhostJacking, an attack that plants malicious instructions inside the security logs and blocked-event alerts AI agents ingest, tricking the agent into executing the attacker's commands word for word.
topics.summary: As enterprises wire AI agents into incident response, the logs those agents read become an injection channel; teams should treat alert and log content as untrusted input and sandbox agent actions.

sources.title: 'GhostJacking' Exposes Identity Governance Gaps in AI Agents
'Ghostjacking' Attack Uses Poisoned Logs to Turn AI Agents Bad

topics.title: LexisNexis Breach and ICE Data Pipeline
topics.latest_developments: LexisNexis pulled its Diligence, Metabase API, and Newsdesk services offline after spotting suspicious activity on servers a third-party vendor hosts, the same day records showed ICE will pay the data broker millions to funnel Americans' personal data into a Palantir system.
topics.summary: LexisNexis aggregates and sells vast troves of personal data to law enforcement including ICE; the outage and the Palantir contract sharpen scrutiny of how much sensitive information the broker holds and where it flows.

sources.title: LexisNexis shuts down services after suspicious activity on servers
ICE to Pay LexisNexis Millions for Data to Feed to Palantir

topics.title: New Attacks Undercut Passkey Protections
topics.latest_developments: Three research teams showed ways to defeat passkeys without cracking their cryptography, reusing signed authentication material Windows exposed, abusing a cloud-synced passkey system from malware already on a machine, and recovering synced private keys.
topics.summary: Passkeys replace passwords and resist phishing, yet these techniques sidestep that protection through exposed credentials and endpoint malware; defenders should harden endpoints and watch for rogue device registration.

sources.title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA

business_politics.title: Nvidia and Wall Street Strike $500 Billion AI Deal
business_politics.latest_developments: Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs formally committed to the financing on August 10, turning last week's plan into a struck agreement.
business_politics.summary: Nvidia and a consortium of Wall Street firms agreed to raise roughly $500 billion to bankroll data centers, the largest private-capital push yet behind the artificial-intelligence build-out.

sources.title: Nvidia, Wall Street Firms Strike AI Financing Deal Targeting $500 Billion
Wall Street giants partner with Nvidia on $500bn AI financing deal

business_politics.title: Oil Surges as Iran Hardens Hormuz Demands
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran demanded a U.S. military withdrawal from the Gulf, the unfreezing of its assets, and war reparations on August 10, prolonging the closure and pushing U.S. stocks off record highs as President Trump reverted to economic pressure.
business_politics.summary: Oil futures rallied and the S&P 500 slipped as Iran's conditions extended the shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, while Ayatollah Ali Khamenei tightened his grip through senior military appointments.

sources.title: Oil Extends Rally With Iranian Demands Delaying Hormuz Deal
U.S. Stocks Fall as Hopes for Strait of Hormuz Reopening Are Dashed Again
Iran's supreme leader tightens grip with top appointments

business.title: Federal Investigators Fault U.S. Steel Over Clairton Blast
business.latest_developments: The U.S. Chemical Safety Board released its findings on August 10, concluding preventable safety and management failures caused the 2025 Clairton Coke Works explosion.
business.summary: Federal investigators concluded U.S. Steel could have prevented the 2025 explosion at its Clairton Coke Works in Allegheny County, citing multiple lapses at the largest coke plant in the region.

sources.title: 'It should never have happened': CSB says preventable failures caused deadly Clairton explosion
U.S. Steel could have prevented 2025 Clairton Coke Works explosion, federal investigators say

business.title: Sherwin-Williams Fined for Beaver County Air Violations
business.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and Sherwin-Williams signed a consent order carrying a $124,700 penalty and corrective steps after air-pollution violations.
business.summary: Sherwin-Williams will pay $124,700 and fix violations of the Air Pollution Control Act at its manufacturing plant in Rochester, Beaver County, after residents said the air smelled of chemicals like nail-polish remover inside their homes.

sources.title: Sherwin-Williams to pay $124,700 penalty after Beaver County residents say air smells of "pure chemicals"

around_town.title: Allegheny County Confronts Pension Shortfall
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported August 10 that the county must contribute $100 million a year for 20 years to close its underfunded pension and has yet to decide how to pay.
around_town.summary: Allegheny County faces a $100-million annual bill for two decades to shore up its underfunded employee pension, and it is searching for answers before turning to taxpayers.

sources.title: Allegheny County searches for answers to fix underfunded pension

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Teacher Shortage Deepens
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported August 10 that Pennsylvania awarded 65% fewer teaching certificates this year than it did a decade ago, a decline a researcher called severe.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania's teacher shortage is squeezing school districts as the state issues 65% fewer teaching certificates than it did ten years ago.

sources.title: Researcher calls Pennsylvania's teacher shortage "severe"

around_town.title: Heavy Rain and Flooding Threaten Western Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: Forecasters declared Tuesday, August 11, an Alert Day, with rounds of heavy rain capable of dropping up to four inches and flooding lingering through Thursday.
around_town.summary: Western Pennsylvania faces strong-to-severe storms and flash flooding this week, with residents in Greensburg pressing for safety changes after recent flooding.

sources.title: Pittsburgh area faces heavy rain and flooding through Thursday
Flooding threat continues Tuesday for western PA

events.title: Whiskey Rebellion Anniversary at Braddock's Battlefield Museum
events.latest_developments: KDKA reported August 10 that the museum will hold its anniversary fundraiser Wednesday, August 12.
events.summary: Braddock's Battlefield History Museum marks the 232nd anniversary of the Whiskey Rebellion on Wednesday, August 12, near North Braddock, with whiskey tastings from local and statewide distilleries, historical reenactments, and food trucks; proceeds preserve the site.

sources.title: Whiskey Rebellion comes back to life at fundraiser for Braddock's Battlefield History Museum

events.latest_developments: NEXTpittsburgh reported August 10 that the venue's final week of concerts runs through its August 15 closing.
events.summary: The Original Pittsburgh Winery closes for good August 15 after a run of farewell concerts, including a set by co-owner Tim Gaber's band, the Buzz Poets; Gaber and co-owner Anthony Jardine urged fans to visit before the doors shut.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported August 10 that the trio remains sidelined ten days into camp.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers are still without cornerback Joey Porter Jr., cornerback Jalen Ramsey, and safety DeShon Elliott at training camp, and the new coaching staff says it is not worried about the injuries.

sources.title: The Steelers defense is still missing 3 of its key pieces, but their new coaching staff isn't concerned

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Off The Bat column on August 10 assessed how the deadline additions reshape the relief corps.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette examined the Pirates' bullpen overhaul after general manager Ben Cherington added right-hander Luke Weaver at the trade deadline, arguing no clear model exists for rebuilding a relief corps midseason.
